name: Plage de Saïdia
hero_subtitle: Morocco’s Blue Pearl: 14 km of fine Mediterranean sand, calm water and a modern marina just one hour from Oujda.

overview.title: The Longest Mediterranean Beach in Morocco
overview.p1: Saïdia is known as the Blue Pearl of the Mediterranean. Its beach stretches for about 14 kilometres of fine golden sand with shallow, calm water that suits families and relaxed swimmers. The resort sits right on the border zone, yet the atmosphere is holiday-friendly and easy-going.
overview.p2: Come for a simple beach day from Oujda (around one hour by grand taxi) or stay overnight in one of the modern resorts. The marina adds restaurants, evening walks and water-sport options, while quieter stretches of sand remain available even in high season.
overview.p3: Unlike the Atlantic coast, the Mediterranean here is usually gentler. That, plus the length of the beach, is why many visitors from eastern Morocco and neighbouring countries return year after year.

moods.title: What to Do at Saïdia, Hour by Hour
moods.subtitle: A beach day works best if you plan around the heat and the light.

1.title: Arrive Early, Claim Your Spot
1.desc: Leave Oujda after breakfast. The sand is cooler, parking is easier and the water is quiet. Perfect for a first swim and photos without crowds.

2.title: Swim, Marina Lunch, Water Sports
2.desc: After a late lunch at the marina (grilled fish, salads), rent a paddleboard or jet-ski if you want activity, or simply rest under an umbrella.

3.title: Sunset Walk and Return or Stay
3.desc: Walk the corniche as the light turns gold. Either head back to Oujda or check into a resort for dinner by the sea.

food.title: What to Eat at Saïdia
food.p1: The marina and seafront restaurants focus on fresh fish and simple Mediterranean plates. Prices are higher than in Oujda medina but still reasonable.
food.li1: Grilled whole fish or calamari with lemon and salad.
food.li2: Seafood platters and simple pasta or pizza for families.
food.li3: Fresh juices and mint tea on café terraces.
food.li4: Ice cream and snacks along the promenade.
food.li5: If you stay overnight, many resorts offer half-board with international and Moroccan options.
food.p2: Check the price of fish before ordering; it is usually sold by weight. Marina restaurants are the most convenient if you arrive by taxi.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Saïdia Beach

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: From Oujda take a grand taxi from the main stations (about 1 hour, shared or private). Agree the price in advance. Some hotels organise transfers.

2.title: Sun and Comfort
2.desc: Bring strong sunscreen, a hat and water. The sand and water heat up quickly from June to September. Umbrellas and loungers are available for rent on the main stretches.

3.title: Safety and Etiquette
3.desc: The beach is generally safe and family-oriented. Keep valuables with you or in a hotel safe. Dress modestly when walking through the town centre away from the resort areas.

q1.question: Is Saïdia beach free?
q1.answer: Yes, the public beach is free to access. You only pay for loungers, umbrellas, food, drinks or water-sport rentals.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit Saïdia?
q2.answer: May to October for swimming. July and August are hottest and busiest. June and September often offer the best balance of warm water and fewer crowds.

q3.question: Is Saïdia safe for families?
q3.answer: Yes. The water is generally calm and shallow near the shore, and the resort atmosphere is family-oriented. Standard precautions with belongings apply.

q4.question: How long should I spend at Saïdia?
q4.answer: A full day is ideal for beach time, lunch and a marina walk. Many visitors also stay one or two nights in a seafront hotel or resort.

q5.question: Can I combine Saïdia with Oujda in one day?
q5.answer: Yes. Spend the morning in Oujda’s medina, then take a grand taxi to Saïdia for the afternoon and early evening before returning.
